 How to Submit Public Comment

 Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following
 methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

 In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City Clerk
 prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the Mayor’
 s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council.

 Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as noted below. Public
 Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record. Words that would disrupt the meeting,
 including profanity, obscenity, and discriminatory language, will not be read. Your comments must be
 received by 5:00 P.M. on meeting day.

  Tuesday, December 5, 2023

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Mayor Harrington
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Harrington, Vice Mayor Wu, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Menchaca

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. EMPLOYEE AWARDS

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of November 7, 2023.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 5, 2023  2
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – OCTOBER 2023

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2023-2024 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 23-36) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2023-2024 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for October 2023.

  D. DEVELOPMENT IMPACT FEE COMPLIANCE REPORT REQUIRED PURSUANT
  TO GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 66006 FOR FY 2022-23

  Pursuant to Government Code Section 66006, a local agency which levies a fee
  subject to Government Code Section 66001 shall make available to the public
  a report providing the information required by Government Code Section
  66006(b)(1) and shall review that information at the next public meeting not
  less than 15 days after the information has been made available to the public.
  The report was publicly available on the City’s website beginning November 17,
  2023. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Annual
  Development Impact Fee Compliance Report for FY 2022-23 in accordance with
  Government Code Section 66006.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 5, 2023  3
   E. ORDINANCE NO. 693: AMENDING CHAPTER 153 OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE, VALLEY BOULEVARD SPECIFIC PLAN, AND MISSION
  DISTRICT SPECIFIC PLAN RELATING TO OBJECTIVE DESIGN STANDARDS
  FOR MULTI-FAMILY AND MIXED-USE PROJECTS (ZTA23-002) – SECOND
  READING AND ADOPTION

  Adoption of Ordinance No. 693 would amend Title XV, Chapter 153 (Zoning
  Code) of the San Gabriel Municipal Code, Valley Boulevard Specific Plan, and
  Mission District Specific Plan relating to objective Design Standards for Multi-
  Family and Mixed-Use Projects. The Fiscal Year 2023-24 Adopted Budget
  includes the cost for required legal publication (Account No. 121-702-00-65-
  000) and codification (Account No. 121-702-00-22-000) of the ordinance.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed
  amendment would be exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
  under section 15061(b)(3) of the CEQA guidelines, under the commonsense
  exemption, because it can be seen with certainty that it would not have a
  significant effect on the environment and, thus, is not subject to CEQA review.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  693 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel,
  California, Approving Planning Case No. ZTA23-002, Amending Title XV,
  Chapter 153 (Zoning), Valley Boulevard Specific Plan, and Mission District
  Specific Plan relating to Objective Design Standards for Multi-Family and
  Mixed-Use Projects.”

  F. ORDINANCE NO. 695: AMENDING CHAPTER 153 OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO ADDRESS MIXED-USE STANDARDS IN THE C-1 AND
  C-3 ZONE DISTRICTS (ZTA 23-003) – SECOND READING AND ADOPTION

  Adoption of Ordinance No. 695 would amend Title XV, Chapter 153 (Zoning
  Code) of the San Gabriel Municipal Code (SGMC) relating to Mixed-Use
  Standards in the C-1 and C-3 Zone Districts

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed
  amendments were reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental
  Quality Act. An Initial Study/Negative Declaration was prepared for the 2021-
  2029 Housing Element, as required by the California Environmental Quality Act,
  Public Resources Code Section 21000 et seq., the CEQA Guidelines, and the City
  of San Gabriel Local Guidelines for Implementing CEQA. The Initial

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 5, 2023  4
   Study/Negative Declaration considered the policies and programs outlined in the
  Housing Element. The Housing element establishes objectives, policies, and
  programs to assist the City in achieving state-mandated housing goals. No formal
  land use changes or physical development are proposed at this time and future
  land use and physical development would require separate environmental
  evaluation.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  695 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel,
  California, Approving Planning Case No. ZTA23-003, Amending Title XV,
  Chapter 153 (Zoning) relating to mixed-use standards in the C-1 and C-3 Zone
  Districts.”

  G. ORDINANCE NO. 698 EXTENDING EXISTING DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT
  FOR PROJECT NO.  PL-15-149, A PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AND
  DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT, AND VESTING TENTATIVE PARCEL MAP NO.
  74993 FOR THE ELEGANCE AT SAN GABRIEL ASSISTED LIVING PROJECT
  AT 806-824 SOUTH GLADYS AVENUE VIA ADOPTION OF FIRST
  AMENDMENT TO THE DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT – SECOND READING
  AND ADOPTION

  Adoption of Ordinance No. 698 would extend the term of the Development
  Agreement, Planned Development and Vesting Tentative Parcel Map for the
  Elegance Project at 806-824 South Gladys Ave. There is no negative fiscal
  impact as it relates to this request for extension. Should the extension not be
  approved, this project would most likely not move forward reducing the
  potential property tax revenue for the City.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The Mitigated
  Negative Declaration adopted in conjunction with the Project remains valid and
  in effect and continues to be the proper and legal environmental document for
  the Project.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive the second reading and adopt by
  title Ordinance No. 698 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City
  of San Gabriel, California, Extending Existing Development Agreement for
  Project No. PL-15-149, a Planned Development and Development Agreement,
  and Vesting Tentative Parcel Map No. 74993 for the Elegance Assisted Living

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 5, 2023  5
   Project at 806-824 South Gladys Avenue via Adoption of First Amendment to
  the Development Agreement.”

  H. APPROVAL OF FINAL PARCEL MAP NO. 82763, A 2-UNIT CONDOMINIUM
  DEVELOPMENT PROJECT LOCATED AT 313 WEST NORWOOD PLACE

  The development project located at 313 West Norwood Place is a 2-unit
  condominium on a 10,018 square-foot-lot. Staff and RKA Consulting Group Inc.,
  the City’s contract consultant for land surveying, have reviewed the Final Parcel
  Map and determined that it is in compliance with the State Subdivision Map
  Act, Conditions of Approval, and the City’s ordinances regarding subdivision.
  There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The project has
  been reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) and is exempt from CEQA based on Section 15332, Class 32 exemption
  (In-Fill-Development).

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Final Parcel Map No. 82763,
  authorize its filing with the Los Angeles County Recorder and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the Subdivision Agreement on behalf of the City.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS – None.

 8. PUBLIC COMMENT

 9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

 11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

 12. ADJOURNMENT

MINUTES OF DECEMBER 5, 2023
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Harrington called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
  7:31 P.M. on Tuesday, December 5, 2023, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South
  Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Harrington.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, Vice Mayor John Wu, and Mayor
  John R. Harrington.
  Council Members Absent:  Denise Menchaca,
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City Attorney
  Paul Early, Community Services Director Rebecca Perez,

I  Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg de Vinck, Fire
  Chief Steven  Wallace,  Human  Resources/Risk
  Management Director Edward Macias, Community
  Development Director Aldo Cervantes, Police Chief
  Edward Elizalde, Finance Director William Kaholokula,
  Assistant City Clerk Marilyn Bonus, and Management
  Assistant Adam Yang.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Assistant City Clerk Bonus provided information for the public on how to view the meeting
  and how to request meeting agendas.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Harrington announced that the Agenda Order was
  approved.

I
  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. EMPLOYEE AWARDS

  City Manager Lazzaretto made the presentation.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Jonathan Hawes provided comments regarding the City of El Monte.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

   Regarding Item 4E, Dylan Casey, California Housing Defense Fund Executive Director,
  provided comments alleging that several provisions in the proposed standards fall
  short of legal requirements.

  A motion was made by Council Member Ding, seconded by Council Member Chan, to
  approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4H as presented.

  Motion carried by a vote of 4-0 as follows:

  NOES:

  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of
  November 7, 2023.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved October 27, 2023, November 2, 2023, November 13,
  2023, and November 16, 2023, Registers of Demands and Warrants for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT - OCTOBER 2023

I  The City Council received and filed the Cash and Investment Report for October
  2023.

  D. DEVELOPMENT IMPACT FEE COMPLIANCE REPORT REQUIRED PURSUANT TO
  GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 66006 FOR FY 2022-23

  The City Council received and filed the Annual Development Impact Fee
  Compliance Report for FY 2022-23 in accordance with Government Code Section
  66006.

  E. ORDINANCE NO. 693: AMENDING CHAPTER 153 OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE, VALLEY BOULEVARD SPECIFIC PLAN, AND MISSION

  MULTI-FAMILY AND MIXED-USE PROJECTS (ZTA23-002)-SECOND READING
  AND ADOPTION

  The City Council waived reading and adopted Ordinance No. 693 entitled, "An
  Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel, California, Approving

I  Planning Case No. ZTA23-002, Amending Title XV, Chapter 153 (Zoning), Valley
  Boulevard Specific Plan, and Mission District Specific Plan relating to Objective
  Design Standards for Multi-Family and Mixed-Use Projects."

  F. ORDINANCE NO. 695: AMENDING CHAPTER 153 OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO ADDRESS MIXED-USE STANDARDS IN THE C-1 AND C-
  3 ZONE DISTRICTS (ZTA 23-003) - SECOND READING AND ADOPTION

  The City Council waived reading and adopted Ordinance No. 695 entitled, "An
  Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel, California, Approving

   Planning Case No. ZTA23-003, Amending Title XV, Chapter 153 (Zoning) relating
  to mixed-use standards in the C-1 and C-3 Zone Districts."

  G. ORDINANCE NO. 698 EXTENDING EXISTING DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT
  FOR PROJECT NO.  PL-15-149, A PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AND
  DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT, AND VESTING TENTATIVE PARCEL MAP NO.
  74993 FOR THE ELEGANCE AT SAN GABRIEL ASSISTED LIVING PROJECT AT
  806-824 SOUTH GLADYS AVENUE VIA ADOPTION OF FIRST AMENDMENT TO
  THE DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT - SECOND READING AND ADOPTION

I  The City Council waived reading and adopted by title Ordinance No. 698 entitled,
  "An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel, California, Extending
  Existing Development Agreement for Project No. PL-15-149, a Planned
  Development and Development Agreement, and Vesting Tentative Parcel Map No.
  74993 for the Elegance Assisted Living Project at 806-824 South Gladys Avenue via
  Adoption of First Amendment to the Development Agreement."

  H. APPROVAL OF FINAL PARCEL MAP NO. 82763, A 2-UNIT CONDOMINIUM

  The City Council approved Final Parcel Map No. 82763, authorized its filing with
  the Los Angeles County Recorder and authorized the City Manager to execute the

  5. PUBLIC HEARING - None.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS - None.

I  7. NEW BUSINESS - None.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT - None.

  9. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto thanked the City Council and community for attending the
  City's Tree-Lighting Event.

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Vice Mayor Wu reported on his attendance at the Asian Pacific Islander (API) Elected
  Officials Summit.

  Council Member Chan reported on his attendance at the Veterans Day and First
  Responders Luncheon and the San Gabriel Turkey Trot Race.

  Council Member Ding thanked the Community Services Department for hosting the

I  City's first Memorial Day Observance event; reported on his attendance at a workshop
  provided by Assemblymember Mike Fong; commented on a Chinese Exclusion Act
  remembrance event, and his trip to Singapore, Malaysia, and Vietnam in relationship
  to learning about refugee history; expressed his appreciation to the United States as
  a first-generation immigrant; and reminded the community to be healthy and safe.

  Mayor Harrington thanked staff for the wonderful and well-attended Tree-Lighting
  event.

  11. CLOSED SESSION - None.
